lesson_title: Demand, Supply and the Drought That Moves Prices
hook_text: A drought hits. Maize meal prices jump. Nobody decided that. So who did?
clip_script: Now our drought. The question says the drought halves the maize harvest. Ask the two exam questions. First: which side of the market is affected — buyers or sellers? The drought struck the farms, the producers. Supply. Second: did the good's own price cause this change? No — weather did. So we are shifting the whole supply curve, not sliding along it. And in which direction? At every possible price, farmers now have less maize to offer. The supply curve shifts leftward. That is the complete diagnosis: demand curve untouched, supply curve shifted left. Half the marks in a market-dynamics question sit in exactly this reasoning.
visual_style: Split screen of cracked farmland and a supermarket price tag, cutting to a clean animated diagram where the supply curve slides left and the price point climbs.
pacing: Dramatic opening seconds, slows into the two-question method, quick punch on the answer.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and draw the whole drought diagram yourself.
